question: A person sells an article for ₹3,450 and earns a profit of 15%. Find the cost price of the article.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

15% Profit = 15/100 = 3/20

Ratio of CP : SP = 20 : (20 + 3) = 20 : 23

Given, 23 units = ₹3,450

1 unit = 3450 ÷ 23 = ₹150

CP = 20 units = 20 × 150 = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹3,450

Profit = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

 
 CP = 100%

 
 SP = 115%

 SP = ₹3450
 
• 

 CP = ?
 
• 

 
• 
 

 + 15% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [3450 × 100] ÷ [100 + 15]

⇒ CP = 345000 ÷ 115

⇒ CP = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Scenario

When an article is sold at a loss, the Selling Price is less than the Cost Price. Formula: CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%].

Marked Price and Discount

The Marked Price (MP) is set above the Cost Price. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Dishonest Dealer Profit

If a dealer sells at cost price but uses a false weight, Profit% = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
